not_found: 882 nm cooling line: isotope shifts for the nine stable isotopes and the 131Xe (and 129Xe) hyperfine constants of 6p[5/2]3 measured in a MOT by Walhout, Megens, Witte, Rolston (Phys. Rev. A 48, R879 (1993)) - only the abstract (no numbers) could be opened; no other open source for A, B of 6p[5/2]3 was found (Husson, Grandin, Kucal, J. Physique 40, 551 (1979), HAL jpa-00209138, is behind a bot wall).
823 nm line isotope shifts (D'Amico et al. 1999): abstract only, no numbers; the 841.15 and 820.86 nm shifts of Bounds et al. are recorded instead.
Absolute optical frequencies of 882 / 823 nm better than NIST: not located.
Directly measured lifetime of 6p[5/2]3 and A values newer than NIST: 33.03 ns is the Vassen-review table value.

Lifetime of 129Xe / 131Xe 3P2 (hyperfine-quenched): the Walhout abstract states it is much shorter in 129Xe but gives no number. Lifetime of the 6s'[1/2]0 clock state (Walhout et al., Opt. Lett. 20, 1192 (1995)) not opened.

Measured Lande g factors beyond NIST ASD: Huet et al. (J. Physique 40, 541 (1979)) covers 6s[3/2]1, 6p'[3/2]1 and 7p levels but the PDF could not be opened; NIST ASD already lists g for the levels drawn.
Experimental reduced matrix elements: none located.
conflicts: 131Xe B(6s[3/2]2): D'Amico et al. 255.7(0.6) MHz vs Bounds et al. 246.7(2) MHz (823 nm) and 259(7) MHz (841 nm); A(131) 705.4(0.4) vs 708.3(1) MHz. The D'Amico values, consistent with the atomic-beam intervals of Faust & McDermott (|A129| = 2384.50 MHz derived), are used.
129Xe A(6s'[1/2]1): D'Amico -5808(2) MHz vs Bounds -5782(4) / -5785(2) MHz (about 25 MHz apart).
3P2 lifetime 42.9(9) s (Walhout 1994) is less than half of the theoretical values (96-150 s); no competing measurement.
notes: Hyperfine entries taken from the comparison table of Bounds et al. are second-hand (method 'compilation', original named in the source); Bounds' own results are listed as alternatives. Isotope-shift keys are kept exactly as printed (pair label 'A-B' with a negative value); see each note on the unverified sign convention. Values converted from mK carry the printed mK numbers alongside. Level energies are NIST ASD values from data/xe/levels.csv; Paschen names in the labels. Entries marked '(abstract)' were read on the publisher's abstract page or HAL record only.
